cohort: A total of 102 antenatal pregnant women aged between 18 and 45 years, divided into a group with PCOS (n=51) and a control group without PCOS (n=51).
finding: Pregnant women with PCOS were more likely to experience complications such as spontaneous abortion, gestational diabetes mellitus, and preterm birth compared to pregnant women without PCOS.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery occurred in 64.7% of women with PCOS compared to 39.2% in the control group, though this difference was not statistically significant.
